title: YRF Entertainment Announces Tunnel Men Series Based on 2023 Uttarkashi Rescue
excerpt: Yash Raj Films' streaming arm is developing a Netflix series about the dramatic 17-day operation that rescued 41 workers from a collapsed Himalayan tunnel, marking the second real-life rescue drama in its partnership with the streamer.
body:
• YRF Entertainment is developing Tunnel Men, a Netflix series inspired by the 2023 Silkyara tunnel rescue in Uttarakhand that trapped 41 workers for 17 days
  • The series will be directed by Ambiecka Pandit and Manan Rawat, with Railway Men director Shiv Rawail returning as showrunner
  • The announcement comes as Aamir Khan separately revealed Silkyara 41, a feature film on the same rescue co-produced with an Australian company
  • The rescue story is the first project under new YRF Entertainment content head Saugata Mukherjee

Yash Raj Films' digital content arm, YRF Entertainment, is developing a new series titled Tunnel Men, based on the 2023 rescue operation that freed 41 workers from a collapsed highway tunnel in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi district. The series will stream on Netflix, extending the production house's partnership with the platform that began with The Romantics in 2023 and continued with The Railway Men.

According to Pinkvilla, Tunnel Men will be directed by Ambiecka Pandit and Manan Rawat, a fresh directorial pairing under the YRF Entertainment banner. Shiv Rawail, who directed The Railway Men, the acclaimed four-part series about the 1984 Bhopal gas tragedy, will serve as showrunner.

From Bhopal to Uttarkashi

The Railway Men, which starred R. Madhavan, Kay Kay Menon, Divyenndu and Babil Khan, told the story of railway employees who risked their lives during the Bhopal disaster. It earned strong reviews for its sensitivity and tight narrative. Tunnel Men follows the same template of dramatising acts of collective heroism during a national crisis.

The Silkyara tunnel rescue gripped India in November 2023. On November 12, a section of the under-construction Silkyara-Barkot tunnel on the Char Dham highway collapsed, trapping 41 construction workers behind roughly 60 metres of debris. What followed was a 17-day operation involving multiple Indian agencies and international experts, culminating in the workers being pulled out through a narrow pipe after traditional drilling machinery repeatedly broke down.

The final breakthrough came from a group of manual "rat-hole miners" who hand-bored through the last stretch of debris after a second auger machine failed with 15 metres remaining. All 41 workers emerged safely on November 28, 2023.

"The writing and pre-production work has been progressing steadily, and the team is aiming to recreate the scale and emotional intensity of the rescue operation."

— Source close to the production, via Pinkvilla

A Race of Two Projects

YRF Entertainment's announcement comes amid a broader rush to dramatise the Uttarkashi rescue. In July 2026, Aamir Khan announced Silkyara 41, a feature film to be directed by Kabir Khan and co-produced with Australia's Mind Blowing Films. Written by Andrew Anastasios, best known for The Water Diviner, the film will also highlight the role of Australian tunnelling expert Arnold Dix, who was part of the international rescue team.

The two projects take different approaches. YRF's Tunnel Men is being developed as a multi-episode series, allowing for a more granular exploration of the rescue timeline. Aamir Khan's Silkyara 41 is a theatrical feature designed for global audiences, announced during PM Modi's visit to Australia as a symbol of bilateral cooperation.

New Leadership at YRF Entertainment

Tunnel Men also marks an important transition for YRF Entertainment. The project is the first major venture under Saugata Mukherjee, who recently joined as Head of Content under CEO Akshaye Widhani. Mukherjee, a veteran of the Indian OTT space, is expected to oversee a push into more original content for the streaming division.

Bollywood Hungama reported that the writing and pre-production work is well underway, though no cast announcements have been made. No release timeline has been confirmed.

Why the Story Resonates

The Uttarkashi rescue became a touchstone of national solidarity in India. The operation brought together engineers, military personnel, disaster management officials and ultimately the rat-hole miners, members of a community whose traditional livelihood is technically banned in India, to pull off what many had feared was impossible. For the Indian diaspora, which followed the rescue in real time through global coverage, the story carries both patriotic and deeply human dimensions. With two major productions now in development, the rescue is set to reach audiences worldwide in competing formats.
